chapter_note: This chapter contains no detectable substrate material. Teaching purity is 0.000. The entire chapter is built around a personal analogy — Mani comparing himself to the sun — which is apostolic/institutional self-identification, not systematic cosmological-correspondential teaching. The sun's behavior (rays extending and withdrawing) serves as a natural analogy for Mani's mission, not as a correspondential map of cosmic domains. No five-fold structures, no zoomorphic-realm mappings, no metal-body or taste-world chains. The chapter is cleanly layered: dialogue frame (¶1), institutional apostolic narrative (¶2-3), and exhortation (¶4). Gardner's synopsis confirms the chapter plays on the title 'enlightener' applied to both the sun and Mani — a hagiographic identification, not a substrate teaching.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic opening: 'Once again he speaks to his disciples' plus setting detail 'in the midst of the congregation.' High dialogue_frame score (31.25). No cosmological content whatsoever.

Describes the sun's rays extending at sunrise and disappearing at sunset. This is a natural observation used as parable/analogy, NOT a systematic cosmological mapping. No correspondential chain (no realm→form, body→metal, taste→world). The imperative 'Note how' is pedagogical voice. The paragraph exists solely to set up ¶3's application to Mani as 'light-giver.' Part of the apostolic self-identification narrative.

Mani applies the sun analogy directly to himself: 'this is also what I am like!' First-person apostolic narrative throughout — 'the image of flesh, wherein I have been set,' 'all my children, the righteous elect who are mine in every country,' 'I will gather together all the elect who have believed in me,' 'I will draw them to me.' This is institutional apostolic material: Mani's incarnation claim, his identification with the sun, his promise to gather the elect. No substrate cosmological mapping.

Seam flag fires correctly. 'Now, because of this I say to you' is a bridge connective from institutional narrative to moral exhortation. Imperative address: 'let him love all my children.' Eschatological promise: 'may live and be victorious... be saved from the black universe.' The cosmic term 'black universe' is embedded in exhortation, not in systematic mapping. Classic devotional closure appended to the apostolic teaching of ¶2-3.
